strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why adversarial training can preserve clean generalization while leaving a large robust generalization gap. Separating clean test, robust training, and robust test errors makes the objective clear.
The decomposition into shared signal learning and training-specific noise memorization offers an interpretable candidate mechanism, with concrete quantities that can be tracked experimentally.

The experiments provide useful descriptive evidence. For example, Table 1 reports a CIFAR10 model with 86.05% clean test accuracy, 99.57% robust training accuracy, and 50.08% robust test accuracy. The additional flatness measurements complement these observations.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider a uniform distribution on (+e1,+1) and (-e1,-1), radius δ=1/2, and the clean classifier f(x)=x1-3/4. This satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3, including constant robust error for the clean classifier. With N=D samples, both support points occur with empirical frequencies approaching 1/2. Consequently, vanishing robust training error forces zero robust population error, contradicting the asserted existence of a CGRO classifier. The assumptions need to exclude such support-coverage cases.

The representation proof has additional substantive gaps. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes, but Lemma 4.5 incorrectly concludes that all training-centered balls are disjoint; same-class balls can overlap, invalidating the subsequent algebraic rewriting. Appendix F also claims arbitrarily small uniform approximation of the generally discontinuous fS by continuous ReLU networks. Softening an indicator does not establish this claim, and the necessary margin or boundary-mass analysis is absent.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish robustness under the paper's definitions. Training attacks modify only the meaningful patch along the signal direction, leaving all noise patches untouched. Definitions 3.2–3.4 instead use full norm balls. Convergence of the restricted adversarial loss cannot establish vanishing robust training error against that larger threat set. This distinction directly affects the claimed CGRO conclusion because the proposed memorization mechanism relies on the untouched noise.

The clean-generalization proof in Appendix E.12 uses incorrect probabilistic reasoning. Cubic Gaussian projections are not sub-Gaussian, so the stated concentration bound is unjustified. Moreover, an aggregate condition V_i=Θ(1) does not imply that every individual noise-weight component has norm Θ(1), as asserted. These steps require replacement and suitable control of scaling and dependence before the clean test guarantee is established.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is also invalid as stated. A constant predictor has zero input-gradient flatness, yet its label-dependent logistic loss can have an empirical mean below its population mean with nonvanishing probability. The bound would incorrectly prohibit this sampling fluctuation. Appendix G does not supply a valid argument resolving this issue.

The synthetic experiment does not satisfy the theorem's perturbation condition: it uses δ=α=10, whereas Assumption 5.7 requires δ<α. At this radius, an allowed attack can erase the entire meaningful signal; because the remaining noise is independent of the balanced label, every classifier has robust population error at least 1/2. Thus, poor robust accuracy does not isolate the proposed learning failure in a setting where robust generalization is achievable. Missing PGD step counts, step sizes, restarts, and variability estimates further limit verification and reproduction.

The significance of the representation lower bound needs clearer positioning. Theorem 4.7 is existential, and Appendix F again constructs linearly separable data, so the claimed extension beyond the cited Li et al. result is not clearly demonstrated. The worst-case bound and model-width experiments also do not establish representation complexity as the cause of the observed behavior. Although the proposed explanatory connection is worthwhile, the unresolved validity issues in the central results prevent acceptance.
